canonical_question: How does the 'slight difference in composition' between simulation (62% Cr) and experiment (Fig 5O) quantitatively impact the predicted radiation resistance?

question_variants.question: How does the 'slight difference in composition' between simulation (62% Cr) and experiment (Fig 5O) quantitatively impact the predicted radiation resistance?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper mentions the slight difference in composition between simulation and experiment might be a kinetic effect due to irradiation modifying the steady-state microstructure. It does not provide a quantitative analysis of how this specific 62% Cr vs experimental composition impact the predicted radiation resistance, nor does it explicitly link the magnitude of the composition difference to a quantitative change in resistance metrics.

answers.answer: The paper attributes the slight difference in composition (simulation vs experiment) to kinetic effects resulting from irradiation modifying the steady-state microstructure. It does not quantify the impact of this specific compositional difference on the predicted radiation resistance beyond this qualitative attribution.
answers.mechanism: Kinetic effect of irradiation on steady-state
evidence_spans: we have systematically carried out first-principles calculations of phase stability and chemical short-range order (SRO) of the multicomponent 38 at % W/36 at % Ta/15 at % Cr/11 at % V alloy as a function of temperature.
The enthalpies of mixing were calculated using the density functional theory (DFT) and CE methods for nearly 270 structures within the BCC underlying crystalline lattice.

In agreement with previous DFT/CE studies for W-Ta and W-V systems ( [33] ), it is found that the enthalpies of mixing for these two binaries are negative for the whole compositional range, a trend followed also by the Cr-V binary.

source_evidence_spans: The slight difference in composition might be a kinetic effect, i.e., a result of the fact that irradiation modifies the steady-state microstructure of the system.
